title: Coolify vs Dokploy and peers, NetBird h2c routing fix, Authentik forward-auth, Origin SSH deploy keys
summary: Self-hosted ops Digest for Sep 13: why Coolify stays the SMB Docker host (Dokploy as the staged alternative), the Traefik gRPC/h2c split that fixes NetBird ManagementService on Coolify, Authentik forward-auth for Coolify apps, and why Origin SSH deploy keys beat GitHub mirrors when the source lives in Origin.

sections.heading: Coolify alternatives for SMB Docker hosting
bullets: Coolify still holds the widest peer match for SMB self-hosting (Compose, one-click catalog, multi-server, backups, teams) plus a documented REST API and MCP server for agent automation. The trade-off is a steady 2026 security-advisory stream, so aggressive patching is part of the job, not an option.

Dokploy is the closest Coolify-like alternative, with Swarm-native multi-node, an API, CLI and official MCP package. It is still pre-1.0 and open-core: SSO, SCIM, custom roles and audit logs sit in the Enterprise editions, per its own Cloud vs Self-Hosted page.

CapRover, Dokku and EasyPanel fit narrower cases: CapRover for simple Swarm apps (source-available license with an appendix, not plain Apache-2.0), Dokku for a CLI-first minimal footprint, EasyPanel for a polished closed-source UI. None is a better wholesale replacement for a typical Coolify setup.

For most SMB teams: stay on Coolify, patch fast, and keep agent automation on the Coolify API/MCP; stage Dokploy on a spare VPS only if Swarm clustering or lighter overhead becomes a real requirement.

sections.heading: NetBird on Coolify — Traefik gRPC/h2c ManagementService fix
bullets: Symptom: clients calling /management.ManagementService/GetServerKey get dashboard HTML, a 404 or a TLS EOF, because Traefik has no h2c router and gRPC falls through to the dashboard catch-all. The dashboard looks healthy while clients stay broken.

Fix per NetBird’s external reverse-proxy docs: for the combined netbird-server container (v0.65.0+), run two Traefik routers, one sending the gRPC service paths to an h2c backend and one sending relay, WebSocket, API and OAuth paths over plain HTTP, with the dashboard as a low-priority catch-all.

Coolify watchouts: let the Coolify Domains UI own dashboard TLS, keep the NetBird hostname DNS-only (no Cloudflare proxy) so gRPC and STUN work, publish UDP 3478 for the embedded STUN server, and re-check custom labels after redeploys.

sections.heading: Authentik Traefik forward-auth for Coolify apps
bullets: Two different jobs: Coolify’s Authentik SSO (OAuth2/OpenID provider, Coolify v4.3.0+) logs people into the Coolify dashboard, while Traefik forwardAuth with an Authentik Proxy provider gates each app before traffic reaches the container.

Coolify’s own guide covers the pattern: an Authentik Proxy provider in forward-auth mode (cookie on the parent domain for cross-subdomain SSO), a shared Traefik middleware pointing at the Authentik outpost, and that middleware attached to each protected app’s HTTPS router.

Watchouts: a broken middleware locks everyone out, so keep the Coolify dashboard on a separate domain and know how to remove the middleware; make sure the outpost is reachable on the proxy’s network, and verify in a private window after each redeploy.

sections.heading: Coolify deploys: Origin SSH deploy keys vs GitHub mirrors
bullets: Coolify now documents a first-class Cursor Origin path: store a private key in Coolify, register the matching public key with origin ssh-key add, then create a Private Repository (with deploy key) resource using the SSH clone URL. HTTPS URLs won’t use the deploy key.

A GitHub mirror buys the GitHub App UX and native webhooks, but it adds a second source of truth that has to be pushed before Coolify sees a commit. Deploy keys clone the real source, with one read-only key per repo and a webhook, API or manual redeploy for auto-deploy.
Rule of thumb: when the app lives in Origin, use Coolify deploy keys and keep a GitHub mirror only when you want GitHub collaboration or non-Coolify CI for its own sake.

sections.heading: What operators should take from this cluster
bullets: A self-hosted PaaS is only as safe as its patch cadence: pick the platform with the automation surface you’ll actually use, then treat its advisory feed as a standing work queue.
Most “it’s up but broken” failures on Coolify are routing and identity edges: gRPC needs h2c, forward-auth needs the right outpost address, and dashboard SSO is not app protection.
Fewer sources of truth means fewer drift incidents: deploy from where the code lives, and add mirrors only on purpose.

bottomLine: For most small teams, Coolify stays the pick as long as you patch aggressively, with Dokploy as the staged alternative only if Swarm or overhead forces the move. Give NetBird a Traefik h2c router for gRPC, gate apps with Authentik forward-auth (separate from dashboard SSO), and deploy Origin-hosted apps with SSH deploy keys instead of mirrors.
